newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania court releases ex-communist, jails others.
newsitem.headline: Albania court releases ex-communist, jails others.

text.p: Albania's appeals court has upheld a Tirana court decision to release a senior ex-communist official charged with crimes against humanity but it quashed a second acquittal, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The appeals court agreed on Monday that Pali Miska, a former politburo member and regional communist chief, was not guilty of crimes against humanity, Gazeta Shqiptare said.
But it overruled the Tirana court's acquittal of Hysen Shahu, a former deputy interior minister, the paper added.

The appeals court left unchanged the sentences of seven other senior party and interior ministry officials, jailed for up to 22 years for crimes against humanity for ordering thousands of dissidents into internal exile before the demise of communism in 1990.
Gazeta Shqiptare said the court did not consider there was sufficient evidence to imprison Miska but it reversed Shahu's acquittal for crimes against humanity.
The prosecution had asked for a 15-year jail terms for both men from the appeals court.
Miska, in prison for abuse of power, should be released in one month.

Around 100,000 Albanians are believed to have been forced into exile in remote villages during 45 years of communist rule because of their opposition to the Stalinist government or for trying to escape from the isolated Balkan country.

Three senior ex-communists were sentenced to death in May but an appeals court revoked the sentences and imposed jail terms instead. Thirteen other ex-communists have been sentenced to up to 25 years in jail for crimes against humanity.
No definite date has yet been set for the trial of former president Ramiz Alia and two former interior ministers charged with ordering the shooting of Albanians who tried to flee the country.
